title: The Huasteca Potosina in November: Long Weekends, Weather, and Waterfalls (Complete 2026 Guide)
metaTitle: Huasteca Potosina in November 2026: Complete Guide
metaDescription: Complete guide to the Huasteca Potosina in November 2026: weather, prices, long weekends, waterfalls, and the best tours. Everything you need to know.
excerpt: November in the Huasteca Potosina brings green jungle, full waterfalls, and 18–28 °C days. Weather, 2026 prices, long-weekend tips, and the best waterfall tours.
contentHtml:
The Huasteca Potosina in November means lush green jungle, waterfalls full from the season's last rains, and temperatures ranging from 18 °C at night to 28 °C during the day, without the stifling heat of summer. Many travelers arrive wondering whether the rains are over or the rivers are still running high. The answer is that November marks the perfect transition: the water still flows strong, and the sky usually opens up into clear days. The Huasteca Potosina in November gives you the best of both worlds: the lush vegetation of a tropical autumn and the comfortable weather of the start of the dry season.

This guide brings together everything you need to plan your trip with 2026 data: admission and tour prices, the best waterfalls for this time of year's water flow, how to make the most of the November long weekend in the Huasteca, and what to expect from Huasteca weather in November day by day. According to the local operators we work with, November long weekends draw many more visitors than regular weeks of the same month, which makes planning ahead essential. If you'd rather travel the Huasteca in the fall with everything arranged from the start, you'll find the most concrete options here too.

At www.huasteca-potosina.com we work with local guides and operators across the region. This guide is updated with real experiences from people who travel the Huasteca Potosina every week. Last updated: November 2026. If you want to arrive with everything sorted, check out our all-inclusive packages to visit the Huasteca Potosina in November.

Huasteca weather in November: what temperatures and rain to expect

What is the weather like in the Huasteca Potosina in November?

Huasteca weather in November means clear skies for most of the day, with occasional rain at dusk on 2 to 4 days out of every 30, according to the area's historical records. Temperatures in Ciudad Valles and Tamasopo hover around 26–28 °C at midday, while in Xilitla, which sits at a higher elevation, the thermometer drops to 16–18 °C in the early morning hours. This temperature gap between the mountains and the plains means the gear you bring makes all the difference to enjoying the trip without hassles.

The groups we coordinate in November confirm that mornings are the clearest: the window from 7:00 AM to 1:00 PM has the best light for photographing waterfalls and taking boat trips. Compare October vs. November weather in our October guide to decide which month suits your trip better.

Dry days vs. rainy days: how to plan your itinerary

The rule of thumb our local guides use is simple: schedule the hardest-to-reach waterfalls, like El Meco Waterfall or the Minas Viejas Waterfalls, for the first few days, when the forecast tends to be more stable. Save tours under cover or in dense jungle for the afternoon. Water activities like rafting on the Tampaón River are just as fun in light rain, but the dirt roads to some lookouts can get slippery after a downpour.

To check river conditions before you head out, local operators post real-time updates. Read our guide to the best time to visit the Huasteca Potosina and see how the region's water cycle works throughout the year.

November long weekend in the Huasteca: waterfalls and tours with 2026 prices

Which tours should you do during the November long weekend in the Huasteca?

The November long weekend in the Huasteca (in 2026 it links November 2, the Monday of Day of the Dead, with the weekend before) is the natural kickoff to the fall high season. Tours leave Ciudad Valles daily between 7:00 and 8:30 AM. People who book less than 72 hours ahead during this long weekend often find the most popular tours sold out, especially rafting and the Tamul Expedition.

The travelers we host during this period describe the Tamul Expedition as the most complete experience of the long weekend: a canoe ride to the foot of Tamul Waterfall (the tallest waterfall in San Luis Potosí, at 105 meters), a swim in the Cueva del Agua cenote, and the sunset show at the Sótano de las Huahuas (478 meters deep), where parrots and swifts return in flocks as night falls. All for $1,550 MXN per person. Book the Tamul Expedition ahead of time to secure your spot for the long weekend.

How much does it cost to visit the Huasteca Potosina in November? 2026 prices

Individual admission prices in November 2026 are: $100 MXN at the Micos Waterfalls (life jacket included), $180 MXN at Edward James's Las Pozas in Xilitla, and $100 MXN at the Sótano de las Golondrinas (Cave of Swallows). Guided tours priced per person start at $900 MXN (the Coffee Trail or Xilo Cave) and go up to $1,950 MXN for Rafting on the Tampaón River, which includes round-trip transportation, full gear, and a certified guide for 14 km of Class III rapids.

If you'd prefer a hassle-free package, the 3-day / 2-night package with a hotel in Xilitla, Huasteca Immersion (Inmersión Huasteca), costs $8,699 MXN per couple. See the packages available for November and compare what each one includes before you book.

The best waterfalls for a fall trip to the Huasteca

November is an ideal month for waterfalls because the flow still holds the volume of the rainy season without the risk of the flash floods of August or September.

El Meco Waterfalls and Stepped Paradise: the fall waterfall routes

The El Meco Waterfalls route combines the main El Meco Waterfall, the Panoramic Lookout, and El Salto Waterfall in a single full-day tour for $1,700 MXN per person. Getting there involves a jungle walk of about 40 minutes from the meeting point, so shoes with non-slip soles are a must. Book El Meco Waterfalls for this long weekend or any November weekend.

The Stepped Paradise tour (Paraíso Escalonado) pairs the Minas Viejas Waterfalls with the Micos Waterfalls in the same day for $1,600 MXN per person. At the Micos Waterfalls you can swim in turquoise pools, and they have a separate admission fee of $100 MXN. Read the complete guide to the Minas Viejas Waterfalls to understand the terrain before you arrive. Book Stepped Paradise at least 48 hours ahead during long-weekend season.

Water Route and Puente de Dios: November must-sees

The Water Route visits Puente de Dios in Tamasopo, a natural rock arch over an emerald-green river, together with the Seven Waterfalls (Siete Cascadas) or the Tamasopo Waterfalls for $1,600 MXN per person. In November, the river level under Puente de Dios lets you swim right beneath the arch. Find out everything about Puente de Dios and how to get there.

For rafting on the Tampaón River, November hits the sweet spot: the Class III rapids, including the famous La Tumba rapid, still have enough force for a truly technical run. The $1,950 MXN per person tour includes round-trip transportation, full safety gear, and a certified guide. Book Rafting on the Tampaón River before the long-weekend spots sell out. Read the complete guide to rafting on the Tampaón to know what to expect on each stretch.

How should you plan your Huasteca Potosina itinerary in November?

The groups we host in November usually have 3 to 5 days available. The key is to split the area into two bases: Ciudad Valles for tours to Tamul, Micos, and the Tampaón, and Xilitla for Las Pozas, the misty mountains, and the jungle tours. Trying to cover both from a single spot means one-way drives of more than 2 hours that eat up the most productive morning hours.

Suggested 3-day itinerary for November

A balanced itinerary starts on the Monday of the long weekend in Ciudad Valles with the Tamul Expedition: canoe, cenote, and the Sótano de las Huahuas at sunset ($1,550 MXN). Tuesday is for Stepped Paradise, with the Minas Viejas and Micos Waterfalls ($1,600 MXN). On Wednesday, transfer to Xilitla (an hour and a half from Ciudad Valles) for the Surrealist Route, with Edward James's Las Pozas, the Huichihuayán Spring (Nacimiento de Huichihuayán), and the Cueva de las Quilas ($1,400 MXN). See the detailed 3-day itinerary to fit it to your budget.

Where should you start, and how do you get around in November?

Ciudad Valles is the most practical gateway: from downtown the main sites are less than 90 minutes away by car. Xilitla is an hour and a half to the south, on a winding mountain road. Avoid that drive at night, especially if it's raining, because fog reduces visibility on some mountain stretches. Check the detailed routes from Mexico City, Monterrey, and San Luis Potosí to pick the most convenient one.

Tips before you visit the Huasteca Potosina in November

  • Book at least 5 days ahead: the November long weekend is the busiest of the fall in the Huasteca. Spots for rafting and the Tamul Expedition sell out fast.
  • Bring quick-dry clothes: you'll be in and out of the water constantly. Soaked cotton is heavy and chilly; go for technical or lycra shirts. See the complete packing checklist for the Potosí jungle before you pack your bag.
  • Have cash on hand in Ciudad Valles: many entrances and shops at the natural sites only take cash. Bring at least $500–$800 MXN in bills on top of everything else for food, tips, and local purchases.
  • Biodegradable sunscreen is required: several sites ask for oxybenzone-free sunscreen so the water stays clean. Regular sunscreen may be turned away at the entrance.
  • Stay in Xilitla for the mountain area: if your itinerary includes La Trinidad, the Cloud Forest (Bosque de Niebla), or the Xilo Cave (Gruta de Xilo), it makes much more sense to spend the night in Xilitla. Find out why it pays to book your Xilitla hotel directly.
  • Keep an eye on your total budget: a 3-day trip with guided tours, basic-tier lodging, and meals runs about $9,000–$11,000 MXN per person. The Huasteca Immersion package, at $8,699 MXN per couple, can end up cheaper: it already includes the hotel, tours, and breakfasts. Work out your detailed budget with our cost guide.

Frequently asked questions about the Huasteca Potosina in November

Is November a good time to visit the Huasteca Potosina?

Yes. The Huasteca Potosina in November offers stable weather, with temperatures of 26–28 °C in the valleys and 16–18 °C in the mountains, occasional rain, and waterfalls with generous flow. It's the transition between the rainy and dry seasons, which pairs green scenery with clear days. According to local operators, it's the second busiest season of the year.

How much does a tour in the Huasteca Potosina cost in November 2026?

Guided tours priced per person cost between $900 MXN (Coffee Trail or Xilo Cave) and $1,950 MXN (Rafting on the Tampaón River). The 3-day/2-night package with a hotel in Xilitla, Huasteca Immersion, costs $8,699 MXN per couple. Separate admission fees, like the Micos Waterfalls, cost $100 MXN per person.

How do you get to the Huasteca Potosina from Mexico City in November?

The most direct route from Mexico City is the highway to Tamazunchale and then on to Ciudad Valles, a drive of 6.5 to 7 h. If your final destination is Xilitla, it's about 7 h from Mexico City, with the last stretch on mountain roads. Avoid arriving in the mountains at night.

Is it safe to travel the Huasteca in the fall with family or as a couple?

Traveling the Huasteca in the fall, in November, is safe with the right planning. Tours run with certified guides, safety gear, and proven routes. For families with kids, tours like Stepped Paradise or the Surrealist Route are more accessible than rafting. Read our road safety tips for the region before you set out.
